scenarios.name: fix-legacy-input-exception-with-jump
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric closely, with InputActionReference move and jump actions enabled in OnEnable and disabled in OnDisable, a gravity and isGrounded jump, input read in Update, and an explanation of the Active Input Handling setting including the Both workaround. B explains the setting and gives a working jump, but it polls Keyboard.current and Gamepad.current directly and never uses InputActionReference or input actions, so it misses the central requirement of the rubric's script and has no OnEnable/OnDisable handling.

scenarios.name: addressables-remote-levels-with-release
scenarios.rationale: Response A matches the rubric closely: it marks level prefabs Addressable in a Remote group, uses InstantiateAsync with a Succeeded check, runs CheckForCatalogUpdates then UpdateCatalogs, unloads with ReleaseInstance, and releases the check handle. Response B covers the remote catalog and release-handle parts well, but it loads scenes with LoadSceneAsync and UnloadSceneAsync instead of prefabs with InstantiateAsync and ReleaseInstance, so it misses the rubric's central loading and unloading elements.

scenarios.name: headless-windows-build-for-ci
scenarios.rationale: Both supply an Editor build method using BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer with EditorApplication.Exit(0/1) and a command line with the required flags, and both mention licence and Windows module. Response A explicitly states the single-instance constraint, which B omits, and A's `-buildTarget StandaloneWindows64` is correct. B adds an extra exit code 2, uses `Win64` as the buildTarget value, and spends a lot of space on a GitHub Actions workflow.
